messages.author: 8298c0d4a543bfba
messages.subject: scale_x_datetime showing two ticks for the same day even when major="1 day"
parts:
I am trying to create a line graph for five days at a time. I have a
continuous y variable, and a date time x variable.

It works well for all dates except when I hit November 07, 2010. It
puts two tick marks for November 07, even though I have major = "1
day"

Any ideas what I've done wrong?

Here is a snippet of my code:
gp<-ggplot()+ opts(axis.title.x=theme_blank()) +
scale_x_datetime(limits = c(as.POSIXct("2010-11-06"),
as.POSIXct("2010-11-10")), minor="1 day")

gpturb<-gp + geom_line(data=dat,aes(x=ReadingDateTime,y=Turbidity),
color="black")+ ylab("Turbidity (NTU)") +
opts(axis.title.y = theme_text(size=12, angle=90))

Thanks for your help

I was able to reproduce the same bug you have by setting my timezone
to 'EST'.

Was able to fix the problem by setting the tz parameter  for scale_x_datetime() to this same timezone,  ie:
scale_x_datetime(limits = c(as.POSIXct("2010-11-06"),

as.POSIXct("2010-11-10")), minor="1 day", tz=Sys.timezone())

Maybe this works for you too.

Have fun,
Frans.

Hi,

I was able to reproduce this bug under Linux by running: 

   TZ='America/New_York'; export TZ

before running R.

Under Linux the fix:

scale_x_datetime(limits = c(as.POSIXct("2010-11-06"),
                as.POSIXct("2010-11-10")), minor="1 day", tz=Sys.timezone())
does not work,  but
scale_x_datetime(limits = c(as.POSIXct("2010-11-06"),

as.POSIXct("2010-11-10")), minor="1 day", tz='EST')
does.


This bug might be triggered by the fact that in the EST timezone day light savings
ended on 07 Nov in 2010.  
Which is right in the given data series,  and it also happens to be the day that is repeated.


Have fun,
Frans.
